content.intro: In this lesson, work through **End-to-End SciPy Project Structure** using the syllabus terms **Organizing reusable modules** and **Keeping configuration separate from computation**. Start from a clearly stated numerical question, choose the smallest appropriate SciPy tool, and inspect the result rather than treating the returned number as self-validating.
content.why_it_matters: End-to-End SciPy Project Structure supports reliable scientific computing by turning a mathematical or data-analysis problem into a repeatable computation. It is useful when you need to choose between methods, understand assumptions, and report limits rather than merely produce a number.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: **End-to-End SciPy Project Structure** is best approached as a deliberate numerical workflow. The supplied curriculum highlights **Organizing reusable modules**, along with **Keeping configuration separate from computation**, **Reproducible execution**, **Automated validation**. Define what the inputs mean and what result would count as credible before increasing problem size or complexity.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about the method
content_blocks.text: Connect the mathematics to the documented API family **end-to-end project structure**. Check input shape and dtype, units and domain assumptions, and whether the method is exact, approximate, iterative, or statistical. The output should be accompanied by an error estimate or a separate check when the API provides one or when the problem allows it.

common_mistakes.problem: Choosing an algorithm before stating the problem and assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Two algorithms that look similar can have different domains, stability, performance, and convergence behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down input shape, units/domain, the quantity to compute, and a validation check before selecting an API.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating returned values as exact truths.
common_mistakes.why: Floating-point arithmetic and iterative numerical algorithms use finite precision and stopping conditions.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect success/status fields and error estimates where available; use scale-appropriate tolerances and independent checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying an example without checking version or edge cases.
common_mistakes.why: Signatures and legacy status can change between releases, and example data rarely covers boundary behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the installed SciPy version, official documentation, input constraints, and a failure case.
